title: 1.1 Interval Notation and Set Notation

icans: I can write inequalities and graphs in interval notation.
I can write sets of numbers in set-builder notation.
I can graph sets of numbers and use the notations for real-life situations.

vocab: writes a set of numbers using its ____________, such as [−2, 5)
the ___________ is included (≤ or ≥, closed circle)
the ___________ is not included (< or >, open circle); always use ( ) with ∞ and −∞
{x | ____________}, read “the set of all x such that …”

blocks.sec: Part 1 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: Brackets and parentheses: A bracket [ ] means the endpoint is _______________; a parenthesis ( ) means it is _______________.

blocks.stem:
Write each inequality in interval notation.
a.  x > 4        b.  −3 ≤ x < 7        c.  x ≤ 0 or x ≥ 5
A number line has a closed circle at −2 and an open circle at 3, with the segment between them shaded. Write the set in interval notation.

notes: Set-builder notation: Set-builder notation: {x | __________} is read “the set of all x _______________.”

blocks.stem:
Write each interval in set-builder notation.
a.  (−5, 1]        b.  [0, ∞)

Write each in interval notation.
a.  x ≤ −6        b.  −1 < x < 8

tickets.stem: A number line has an open circle at 5 and is shaded to the left. Write the set in interval notation.
